note: Hand-authored, Basic-OP subset only (see the scopeNote in ../specs.json). `quote` is verbatim from https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html with line wrapping removed and nothing else changed.

requirements.quote: iss: REQUIRED. Issuer Identifier for the Issuer of the response. The iss value is a case-sensitive URL using the https scheme that contains scheme, host, and optionally, port number and path components and no query or fragment components.
requirements.applies: libs/fastify/plugins/jwt (signIdToken) — the ID Token iss is the same resolved issuer the discovery documents publish.

requirements.quote: sub: REQUIRED. Subject Identifier. A locally unique and never reassigned identifier within the Issuer for the End-User, which is intended to be consumed by the Client. It MUST NOT exceed 255 ASCII [RFC20] characters in length.
requirements.applies: libs/fastify/plugins/jwt (signIdToken) — the user id, a UUID, is well inside 255 ASCII characters and is never reassigned.

requirements.quote: aud: REQUIRED. Audience(s) that this ID Token is intended for. It MUST contain the OAuth 2.0 client_id of the Relying Party as an audience value.
requirements.applies: libs/fastify/plugins/jwt (signIdToken) — the client_id of the client that redeemed the authorization code.
requirements.evidenceMatch: all required claims|audience does not match the relying party

requirements.quote: exp: REQUIRED. Expiration time on or after which the ID Token MUST NOT be accepted by the RP when performing authentication with the OP. iat: REQUIRED. Time at which the JWT was issued.
requirements.applies: libs/fastify/plugins/jwt (signIdToken) — both are emitted as epoch seconds.

requirements.quote: auth_time: Time when the End-User authentication occurred. When a max_age request is made or when auth_time is requested as an Essential Claim, then this Claim is REQUIRED; otherwise, its inclusion is OPTIONAL.
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/routes/oauth/token.ts — the authorization code carries auth_time in epoch milliseconds and the token endpoint threads it into the ID Token as epoch seconds (#310).

requirements.quote: If present in the Authentication Request, Authorization Servers MUST include a nonce Claim in the ID Token with the Claim Value being the nonce value sent in the Authentication Request.
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/routes/oauth/token.ts — the nonce is stored on the authorization code and passed through to signIdToken unmodified.

requirements.quote: Authorization Servers MUST support the use of the HTTP GET and POST methods defined in RFC 7231 [RFC7231] at the Authorization Endpoint.
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/routes/oauth/authorize.ts — GET and POST share one handler.

requirements.quote: none: The Authorization Server MUST NOT display any authentication or consent user interface pages. An error is returned if an End-User is not already authenticated or the Client does not have pre-configured consent for the requested Claims or does not fulfill other conditions for processing the request. The error code will typically be login_required, interaction_required, or another code defined in Section 3.1.2.6 (Authentication Error Response).
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/routes/oauth/authorize.ts — prompt=none returns the error on the client's redirect_uri instead of bouncing to /ui/login (#318), on both the unauthenticated and the step-up paths.

requirements.quote: In addition to the response parameters specified by OAuth 2.0, the following parameters MUST be included in the response: id_token — ID Token value associated with the authenticated session.
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/routes/oauth/token.ts — an id_token is minted whenever the granted scope includes openid.

requirements.quote: at_hash: OPTIONAL. Access Token hash value.
requirements.reason: OPTIONAL for the Authorization Code Flow, and QAuth does not emit it. It is REQUIRED only where an ID Token is returned from the authorization endpoint alongside an access token, which is the hybrid and implicit flows — see the §3.3.2.11 row.

requirements.quote: Clients MUST validate the ID Token in the Token Response in the following manner.
requirements.reason: A relying-party obligation. QAuth's side of it is the signature and the claim set, carried by the §2 rows; that a third-party RP can complete this validation against QAuth's published JWKS is the OIDF Basic OP run's job, tracked by the manual RS256 row in oidc-discovery-1_0.json.

requirements.quote: If the ID Token is issued from the Authorization Endpoint with an access_token value, which is the case for the response_type value code id_token token, this is REQUIRED; otherwise, its inclusion is OPTIONAL.
requirements.reason: Hybrid Flow only. QAuth advertises response_types_supported: ['code'] and implements neither the hybrid nor the implicit flow, so no ID Token is ever issued from the authorization endpoint and neither at_hash nor c_hash can be required.

requirements.quote: The Access Token obtained from an OpenID Connect Authentication Request MUST be sent as a Bearer Token, per Section 2 of OAuth 2.0 Bearer Token Usage [RFC6750].
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/routes/oauth/userinfo.ts — GET and POST both resolve the token from the Authorization header, and POST additionally from a form-encoded body; a query-string token is rejected.

requirements.quote: The sub (subject) Claim MUST always be returned in the UserInfo Response.
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/routes/oauth/userinfo.ts — sub is unconditional; every other claim is scope-gated.

requirements.quote: If a Claim is not returned, that Claim Name SHOULD be omitted from the JSON object representing the Claims; it SHOULD NOT be present with a null or empty string value.
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/routes/oauth/userinfo.ts — a user with no verified email gets the email claim keys absent, never null (#229).

requirements.quote: If the UserInfo Response is signed and/or encrypted, then the Claims are returned in a JWT and the content-type MUST be application/jwt.
requirements.reason: QAuth never offers a signed or encrypted UserInfo response: userinfo_signing_alg_values_supported is intentionally absent from discovery and client registration accepts no signing preference, so no client can request one and the JWT branch is unreachable.

requirements.quote: Support for the request parameter is OPTIONAL. The request_parameter_supported Discovery result indicates whether the OP supports this parameter. Should an OP not support this parameter and an RP uses it, the OP MUST return the request_not_supported error.
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/schemas/oauth.ts — authorizeQuerySchema is a plain z.object with default strip and has no request field, so the parameter is silently dropped rather than rejected.
requirements.reason: QAuth advertises request_parameter_supported: false, so a conformant RP never sends the parameter and the certification suite's request-object modules skip. Returning the error would mean giving the schema a field solely to reject it, and the honest signal — the advertised false — is already there. This becomes a real gap only if request objects are implemented, at which point the flag flips instead.

requirements.quote: The request_uri_parameter_supported Discovery result indicates whether the OP supports this parameter. Should an OP not support this parameter and an RP uses it, the OP MUST return the request_uri_not_supported error.
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/schemas/oauth.ts — same strip; apps/auth-server/src/app/helpers/discovery.ts states request_uri_parameter_supported: false explicitly, because an omitted flag defaults to true.
requirements.reason: Same call as §6.1, with one extra edge: the OIDC default for this flag is true, so silence would have been a false capability claim. #286 fixed that by publishing false on both documents. The error itself is still not returned. Note that a request_uri is a spec MUST under the HAIP profile, so this row is the one most likely to move.
